content:
The long-awaited "Ted Lasso" has finally returned, with the first episode of the show's fourth season now available on Apple TV for subscribers to watch.

"Ted Lasso" finally makes its comeback

More than three years after the third season finale aired, the first episode of the fourth season is now available for streaming on Apple TV.

Apple is pulling out all the stops to promote the show's return, including a surprise appearance by Jason Sudeikis and Brendan Hunt — reprising their roles as Ted and Coach Beard — during the World Cup final, as well as a lookalike contest scheduled for this Thursday (August 6) at the Apple Fifth Avenue Plaza in New York.

If you've managed to avoid any spoilers about the show's return and would like to keep it that way, I suggest you go watch the first episode right now. But if you don't mind getting a general idea of what this season has in store, here's the season synopsis provided by Apple TV:

"Ted Lasso" season four will consist of 10 episodes, airing through October 7, 2026, and is expected to be the first installment of a new three-season story arc.

Most of the main cast is returning, with new additions including Tanya Reynolds (of "Underdogs") and Paloma Cinco (of "De La Cruz"), who is the real-life older sister of Cristo Fernandez — the fan-favorite Dani Rojas, now a professional footballer on the show.

Check out the trailer for the new season of "Ted Lasso" below:

Apple TV costs $12.99 per month, or you can bundle it through an Apple One subscription. The platform offers plenty of other popular shows and movies, including "Severance," "The Studio," "The Morning Show," "Shrinking," and "Silo."
